payload.slides_filled:
Every story's evidence side is filled from the built system (run-82361b2e37e9: 165 tests, 163 pass, 0 fail, typecheck clean).

S1 THE CLEAN CLOSE (killer) - filled. A close tags first, merges with two parents, and leaves a trunk tree carrying the claims and none of the events, on disk or in the tree.
S2 THE AUDIT A YEAR LATER (killer) - filled. Every milestone's evidence is readable through the tag after the close, asserted per milestone rather than only for the last, and the grant now carries the tag so the pointer resolves.
S3 THE INTERRUPTED ITERATION - filled. A blessed gate commits the milestone to the branch and leaves the tree clean; nothing to commit is legal.
S4 THE SHIP THAT REFUSES (killer) - filled. An empty branch refuses and trunk's HEAD is unchanged with no merge pending; the same holds when the tag cannot be created and when a live claim conflicts.
S5 THE ARCHIVE STAYS VISIBLE - filled. The grant index survives the filter while the iteration's own files are gone.
S6 THE WORKTREE THAT CAN VERIFY ITSELF - filled, and its design changed under evidence: the toolchain is now INSTALLED into the worktree rather than linked to a shared one, because a link is a path a removal follows.

ONE FINDING, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN BURIED: the build changed materially AFTER its gate was blessed. Filling S1 against the real system exposed that shipMerge was invoked only by tests - nothing in the engine ever called it. So an iteration could pass its final gate, be marked shipped, and leave the repository untouched, which is precisely what i8c did and what my earlier diagnosis (an empty branch) only half-explained. The close is now wired into the bless path, where iterations actually close, so it runs for every channel including the board. Two further defects fell out of that wiring and were fixed: the milestone commit was silently refusing on the self-hosted repo (SE-C-001, swallowed by a bare catch - it now runs under the same allowSelf policy as the rest of the worktree lane and reports failures instead of hiding them), and a type narrowing hid the closed-state check. Three existing suites were reconciled to the new reality - the close now happens at the final bless, so tests that shipped by hand afterwards were rewritten to assert the bless's own split.
payload.demos_seeded:
Two killer demonstrations, one automated and one owed live.

DEMO 1 - THE FULL SHIP PATH, automated and permanent: a fixture iteration is provisioned, walked through the loop, and blessed at its final gate; nobody calls shipMerge. The check then asserts trunk actually moved, the tag exists, the live claim is on trunk, the event is not, and the evidence is readable through the tag. This is the demonstration that would have caught i8c's silent non-ship, and it is now a permanent acceptance scenario rather than a one-off.

DEMO 2 - THE SPLIT ON THIS REPOSITORY, owed at M9 and honestly bounded: i5d's own close is the first real one. It carries a bootstrap constraint worth stating plainly - the running engine is trunk's, which predates this iteration, so i5d's own ship cannot use the code i5d adds unless the close is driven from the built engine deliberately. That is the same bootstrap shape i5b recorded when it ran on trunk, and it will be recorded as such rather than presented as a clean self-demonstration.

EXECUTABLE SLICES CONVERTED: the ship-path demonstration, the empty-branch refusal, the untaggable refusal, the conflict abort, and per-milestone reachability are all permanent checks in the battery. The one slice that stays manual is the owner-physical case, and there is none in this iteration.
